records.literal_gloss: It came about then on a Sabbath [that] to be passing through him through grainfields, and were plucking the disciples of him and were eating the heads of grain, rubbing [them] in the hands.

en.L: Now it happened on a Sabbath [that] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was passing through grainfields, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples were plucking and eating the heads of grain, rubbing [them] in [their] hands.
en.B: On a Sabbath Jesus was walking through fields of grain. His disciples were pulling off heads of grain, rubbing them between their hands, and eating them.
en.R: One Sabbath day Jesus was walking through some fields of grain. His disciples picked some heads of grain. They rubbed them in their hands to get the seeds out, and they ate them.

es.L: Y sucedió que un sábado pasaba {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} por unos sembrados, y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos arrancaban espigas y se las comían, frotándolas con las manos.

fr.L: Or il arriva, un jour de sabbat, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} traversait des champs de blé, et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples arrachaient et mangeaient les épis, en [les] frottant dans [leurs] mains.
fr.B: Un jour de sabbat, Jésus passait à travers des champs de blé. Ses disciples arrachaient des épis, les froissaient entre leurs mains et en mangeaient les grains.
fr.R: Un jour de sabbat, Jésus marchait à travers des champs de blé. Ses disciples ont cueilli des épis. Ils les ont frottés dans leurs mains pour en faire sortir les grains, et ils les ont mangés.

vi.R: Vào một ngày Sa-bát, Đức Giê-xu đi ngang qua mấy đồng lúa. Các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bứt mấy bông lúa. Họ lấy tay vò cho hạt lúa rơi ra, rồi ăn.

ko.L: 안식일에 [이런] 일이 있었다. 그분이 곡식밭 사이로 지나가고 계셨는데, 그분의 제자들이 이삭을 잘라 손으로 비비면서 먹고 있었다.
ko.B: 어느 안식일에 예수께서 곡식밭 사이로 지나가고 계셨다. 제자들은 이삭을 잘라 손으로 비벼 먹고 있었다.
ko.R: 어느 안식일에 예수께서 곡식밭 사이로 걸어가고 계셨다. 제자들은 곡식 이삭을 땄다. 그리고 낟알이 나오도록 손으로 비벼서 먹었다.

decisions.choice: on a Sabbath: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: on the second-first Sabbath, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts, including most later ones, read "on the second-first Sabbath", using a word found nowhere else in Greek writing. Its meaning is unknown: perhaps the second Sabbath of a series, or the first Sabbath after Passover. Several early manuscripts lack the word, and it may have begun as a note in the margin. The meaning of the verse is the same either way. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Sabbath: the seventh day, from sunset on Friday to sunset on Saturday, set apart by God's law as a day of rest
decisions.reason: The commandment forbids work on the seventh day (Exodus 20:8-11), even at harvest time (Exodus 34:21). How to keep it was a constant question for devout Jews.

decisions.choice: plucking and rubbing heads of grain: allowed by the law on other days
decisions.reason: The law let a passer-by pick heads of grain by hand in a neighbor's field, though not use a sickle (Deuteronomy 23:25). The question in 6:2 is about the day, not the field: picking and rubbing grain could be counted as reaping and threshing.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section.

decisions.choice: to get the seeds out
decisions.reason: Readable says why they rubbed the grain: to free the kernels from the husks.

decisions.choice: sábado; R adds "el día de descanso"
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts. Spanish "sábado" is also the everyday name for Saturday, so Readable says once what the day was (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: spans only where Spanish writes the pronoun (él, sus)
decisions.reason: Where the English marks "he" for Jesus, Spanish usually needs no pronoun at all ("pasaba", "dijo"), and a clitic joined to the verb ("acusarlo") takes none, so Spanish has fewer deity_pronoun spans than English throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level, David's story (6:3-4) and the house-builders (6:48-49) included
decisions.reason: As in John and Mark: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken and read in school today. What Jesus says keeps the tenses of speech, so the story of David he retells is in the passé composé. Literal renders Luke's "it came about that" as "il arriva que". This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: un jour de sabbat, le sabbat (lowercase)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's form for the New Testament: "sabbat" is a common noun in French and takes no capital. "Samedi" would lose the day's religious meaning (m2).

decisions.choice: spans only on free pronouns and possessives (wake)
alternatives: a span for every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: As in John and Matthew: Swahili marks most pronouns for Jesus inside the verb ("alikuwa akipita"), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so only free pronouns and possessives carry the deity_pronoun span. Swahili has fewer spans than English throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: kufikicha
decisions.reason: "Kufikicha" is the Swahili word for rubbing ears of grain between the hands to free the kernels, exactly what the disciples did (meaning decision m3); "kusugua" is any rubbing or scrubbing.

decisions.choice: "đồng lúa", "bông lúa" for the grainfields and heads of grain
decisions.reason: As in the parallel Mark 2:23: "lúa" in the general sense of grain; "ruộng" suggests wet rice paddies and "lúa mì" names wheat only.

decisions.choice: "{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}" for Jesus in the narrative, "Ta" when he speaks of himself (whole chapter)
decisions.reason: The forms the style guide sets for the Gospels, as in the Vietnamese Mark and Luke 4-5; a pronoun at the start of a sentence is written plainly with its capital.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean, through Luke 6; the narrative honours Jesus with "께서" and -시-, Literal refers to him as "그분", Jesus speaks in 해라체 and people speak to him in 합쇼체
alternatives: Korean spans for pronouns referring to Jesus
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change (Korean style guide, sections 4 and 7), as in Luke 5 in Korean.

decisions.choice: "곡식밭" for the grainfields; "이삭" for the heads of grain; "[이런] 일이 있었다" (L) for "it came about"
decisions.reason: The Greek names sown fields without naming the crop, as in Mark 2:23 in Korean. Literal keeps Luke's opening formula with the subject Korean needs in brackets, as in Luke 5:12 and 5:17.

source.text: τινὲς δὲ τῶν Φαρισαίων εἶπαν· Τί ποιεῖτε ὃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν τοῖς σάββασιν;

records.literal_gloss: Some then of the Pharisees said, Why are you doing what not is lawful on the Sabbaths?

en.L: But some of the Pharisees said, "Why are you doing what is not lawful on the Sabbath?"
en.B: Some of the Pharisees said, "Why are you doing something the law forbids on the Sabbath?"
en.R: Some of the Pharisees said, "Why are you doing something that the law does not allow on the Sabbath day?"

es.L: Pero algunos de los fariseos dijeron: «¿Por qué {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} lo que no es lícito en sábado?».
es.B: Algunos de los fariseos dijeron: «¿Por qué {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} algo que la ley prohíbe en sábado?».
es.R: Algunos de los fariseos dijeron: «¿Por qué {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} algo que la ley no permite en sábado?».

fr.L: Mais quelques-uns des Pharisiens dirent : « Pourquoi faites-vous ce qui n’est pas permis le jour du sabbat ? »
fr.B: Quelques Pharisiens dirent : « Pourquoi faites-vous, le jour du sabbat, ce que la Loi interdit ? »
fr.R: Quelques Pharisiens ont dit : « Pourquoi faites-vous une chose que la Loi ne permet pas le jour du sabbat ? »

ko.L: 그러자 바리새파 사람들 가운데 몇 사람이 말했다. "어찌하여 너희는 안식일에 해서는 안 되는 일을 하느냐?"
ko.B: 바리새파 사람 몇이 말했다. "너희는 왜 안식일에 율법이 금하는 일을 하느냐?"
ko.R: 바리새파 사람 몇 명이 말했다. "너희는 왜 안식일에 율법이 허락하지 않는 일을 하느냐?"

decisions.choice: Pharisees: a movement of Jews devoted to keeping God's law in every part of life
decisions.reason: The Pharisees were respected teachers who kept the law strictly, together with the traditions handed down about how to keep it (Mark 7:3). Paul had been one (Philippians 3:5). They often watched and questioned Jesus (5:17, 21, 30).

decisions.choice: you: plural, spoken to the disciples
decisions.reason: The verb is plural. In Luke they question the disciples, and Jesus answers for them (6:3).

decisions.choice: what is not lawful: work forbidden on the Sabbath
decisions.reason: Picking and rubbing grain counted as reaping and threshing, which the law forbade on the Sabbath (Exodus 34:21). Later Jewish teaching lists reaping and threshing among the main kinds of forbidden work.

decisions.choice: on the Sabbaths: a plural form meaning the Sabbath day
decisions.reason: The plural is often used for a single Sabbath (4:31; 13:10).

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}}
decisions.reason: The Pharisees speak to the disciples as a group (meaning decision m2), so the plural "you" is the reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain). The same for every plural "you" in the chapter, through the whole sermon in 6:20-49.

decisions.choice: les Pharisiens, capitalised; "vous" (plural) to the disciples; la Loi (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet capitalises the names of Jewish groups, as in John and Mark. The Greek verb is plural (m2), so French says "vous". Balanced and Readable name the Law of Moses as "la Loi", with a capital, as the term sheet does.

decisions.choice: "các anh" for the disciples in the Pharisees' question
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says "you" is plural and spoken to the disciples; "các anh" is the polite but cool word between grown men who are not friends, as the Pharisees use it in 5:30.

decisions.choice: The Pharisees speak to the disciples in 해라체 with "너희"
decisions.reason: The Greek "you" is plural and addressed to the disciples (meaning decision); teachers of the law speak down to a rival teacher's disciples, as in Luke 5:30 and Mark 2:16 in Korean.

source.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Οὐδὲ τοῦτο ἀνέγνωτε ὃ ἐποίησεν Δαυὶδ ὁπότε ἐπείνασεν αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ μετ’ αὐτοῦ ὄντες;

en.B: Jesus answered them, "Have you not even read about what David did when he and the men with him were hungry?
en.R: Jesus answered them, "Have you not read in the Scriptures what David did? He and his men were hungry.

vi.L: Và Đức Giê-xu trả lời họ: "Các người chưa từng đọc điều này sao, là điều Đa-vít đã làm khi ông đói, ông và những người ở với ông,
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu trả lời họ: "Các người chưa đọc việc Đa-vít đã làm khi ông và những người đi theo ông bị đói sao?
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời họ: "Các người chưa đọc trong Kinh Thánh việc Đa-vít đã làm sao? Lúc ấy ông và những người đi theo ông đều đói.

ko.L: 그러자 예수께서 그들에게 대답하여 말씀하셨다. "다윗과 그와 함께 있던 이들이 굶주렸을 때에 다윗이 한 일, 이것조차 너희는 읽지 못했느냐?
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 대답하셨다. "다윗과 그 일행이 배고팠을 때 다윗이 한 일을 너희는 읽어 보지도 못했느냐?
ko.R: 예수께서 그들에게 대답하셨다. "너희는 성경에서 다윗이 한 일을 읽지 못했느냐? 다윗과 그와 함께 있던 사람들은 배가 고팠다.

decisions.choice: what David did: 1 Samuel 21:1-6
decisions.reason: Fleeing from Saul, David came to the priest Ahimelech at Nob and asked for food. The only bread there was the holy bread that had been taken from the LORD's table, and the priest gave it to David for himself and his men.

decisions.choice: have you not even read this: a question that expects the answer yes
alternatives: a real question about what they had read
decisions.reason: The words "not even" make the question sharp: men who study the Scriptures have surely read this story, yet they have missed its point.

decisions.choice: in the Scriptures
decisions.reason: Readable says where they would have read it.

decisions.choice: two sentences: the question, then David's hunger
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the question short and tells the story in the following sentences.

decisions.choice: Jesus speaks to the Pharisees as "các người" (6:3-9)
decisions.reason: The style guide's form for Jesus speaking to opponents, as in the parallel Mark 2:25 and Luke 5:22.

decisions.choice: "다윗이 한 일, 이것조차 너희는 읽지 못했느냐?" (L)
decisions.reason: Korean puts the verb last, so Literal names "what David did" first and picks it up with "이것" (this), keeping the Greek's "not even this" and the question that expects yes (meaning decision).

source.text: ὡς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοὺς ἄρτους τῆς προθέσεως λαβὼν ἔφαγεν καὶ ἔδωκεν τοῖς μετ’ αὐτοῦ, οὓς οὐκ ἔξεστιν φαγεῖν εἰ μὴ μόνους τοὺς ἱερεῖς;

records.literal_gloss: how he entered into the house of the God and the loaves of the presentation having taken ate and gave to those with him, which not it is lawful to eat except only the priests?

en.L: how he entered into the house of God, and taking the loaves of the presentation, he ate and gave [some] to those with him, which it is not lawful to eat except for the priests alone?"
en.B: He went into the house of God, took the bread set out before God, and ate it, and he gave some to the men with him. Yet the law allows no one but the priests to eat that bread."
en.R: David went into the house of God and took the special bread that was placed there before God. He ate it, and he gave some to his men. But the law said that only the priests could eat that bread."

es.L: cómo entró en la casa de Dios y, tomando los panes de la presentación, comió y dio a los que [estaban] con él, los cuales no es lícito comer sino solo a los sacerdotes?».
es.B: Entró en la casa de Dios, tomó los panes consagrados que se ponían delante de Dios y comió, y también les dio a los hombres que iban con él. Sin embargo, la ley no permite que nadie coma ese pan, sino solo los sacerdotes».
es.R: David entró en la casa de Dios y tomó el pan especial que estaba allí delante de Dios. Comió de ese pan y les dio también a sus hombres. Pero la ley decía que solo los sacerdotes podían comerlo».

fr.L: comment il est entré dans la maison de Dieu et, ayant pris les pains de la présentation, en a mangé et en a donné à ceux [qui étaient] avec lui, [des pains] qu’il n’est permis de manger qu’aux seuls prêtres ? »
fr.B: Il est entré dans la maison de Dieu, il a pris les pains déposés devant Dieu, il en a mangé et il en a donné aux hommes qui l’accompagnaient. Pourtant la Loi ne permet à personne d’en manger, sauf aux prêtres. »
fr.R: David est entré dans la maison de Dieu. Il a pris le pain spécial qu’on avait placé là, devant Dieu. Il en a mangé, et il en a donné à ses hommes. Pourtant, la Loi disait que seuls les prêtres pouvaient manger ce pain. »

sw.L: jinsi alivyoingia katika nyumba ya Mungu, na akiisha kuitwaa mikate ya kuwekwa mbele [za Mungu], akala, akawapa na wale [waliokuwa] pamoja naye, ambayo si halali kuila isipokuwa makuhani peke yao?"
sw.B: Aliingia katika nyumba ya Mungu, akaichukua mikate mitakatifu iliyowekwa mbele za Mungu, akala, akawapa na watu aliokuwa nao. Lakini sheria haimruhusu mtu yeyote kuila isipokuwa makuhani peke yao."
sw.R: Daudi aliingia katika nyumba ya Mungu, akachukua mikate maalum iliyokuwa imewekwa pale mbele za Mungu. Akala, akawapa na watu wake. Lakini sheria ilisema kwamba ni makuhani tu walioruhusiwa kula mikate hiyo."

vi.L: thể nào ông đã vào nhà Đức Chúa Trời, lấy các ổ bánh bày ra [trước Đức Chúa Trời] mà ăn, và cũng cho những người ở với ông, là bánh không ai được phép ăn ngoại trừ một mình các thầy tế lễ?"
vi.B: Ông đã vào nhà Đức Chúa Trời, lấy bánh bày ra trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời mà ăn, và cho cả những người đi theo mình nữa. Thế mà luật pháp chỉ cho phép các thầy tế lễ ăn bánh ấy thôi."
vi.R: Đa-vít đã vào nhà của Đức Chúa Trời và lấy thứ bánh đặc biệt đã được dâng cho Đức Chúa Trời. Ông ăn bánh đó, và còn chia cho những người đi theo mình nữa. Nhưng luật pháp nói chỉ các thầy tế lễ mới được ăn bánh đó."

ko.L: 곧 그가 어떻게 하나님의 집에 들어가서, 제사장들 말고는 먹어서는 안 되는 차려 놓은 빵을 가져다 먹고, 자기와 함께 있던 이들에게도 주었는지를 [읽지 못했느냐]?"
ko.B: 다윗은 하나님의 집에 들어가서 하나님 앞에 차려 놓은 빵을 가져다 먹고, 함께 있던 사람들에게도 주었다. 그러나 율법은 제사장들 말고는 아무에게도 그 빵을 먹지 못하게 한다."
ko.R: 다윗은 하나님의 집에 들어가서 하나님께 바친 특별한 빵을 가져다 먹었다. 그리고 함께 있던 사람들에게도 나누어 주었다. 그러나 율법에 따르면 그 빵은 제사장들만 먹을 수 있었다."

decisions.choice: the house of God: the tent of worship, then standing at Nob
decisions.reason: The temple had not yet been built in David's day. The tent of worship, the tabernacle, was then at Nob (1 Samuel 21:1).

decisions.choice: the loaves of the presentation: the twelve loaves set out before the LORD
decisions.reason: Every Sabbath twelve fresh loaves were set in two rows on the table in the holy place, before the LORD. The old loaves were holy and were to be eaten only by the priests, in a holy place (Leviticus 24:5-9; Exodus 25:30).

decisions.choice: which it is not lawful to eat: Scripture tells of David's act without condemning it
decisions.reason: The argument runs from the greater case: if David and his men were not condemned for eating the holy bread when they were hungry, the disciples of the one greater than David are not condemned for picking grain. 6:5 states the claim behind it.

decisions.choice: a statement, not the end of the question
decisions.reason: The Greek question runs on from 6:3. Balanced and Readable tell the story as statements, which is easier to follow.

decisions.choice: the bread set out before God (B); the special bread that was placed there before God (R)
decisions.reason: The phrase means bread set out in God's presence. Balanced and Readable say so in plain words.

decisions.choice: los panes de la presentación (L); los panes consagrados (B); el pan especial (R)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 12:4. "Proposición" once meant setting something out, but readers now take it as a proposal; "presentación" keeps the picture of bread set out before God (meaning decision m2). Balanced and Readable say what the bread was, as the English does.

decisions.choice: mikate ya kuwekwa mbele [za Mungu] (L); mikate mitakatifu (B); mikate maalum (R)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 12:4: the Greek names the bread by its being set out before God (meaning decision m2). Literal says that in plain words; Balanced calls it holy bread and Readable special bread, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "các ổ bánh bày ra [trước Đức Chúa Trời]" (L); "bánh bày ra trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời" (B); "thứ bánh đặc biệt đã được dâng cho Đức Chúa Trời" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the parallel Mark 2:26: the older term "bánh trần thiết" is no longer understood by most readers; the plain words say what the bread was.

decisions.choice: "차려 놓은 빵" (L); "하나님 앞에 차려 놓은 빵" (B); "하나님께 바친 특별한 빵" (R)
decisions.reason: The words of Mark 2:26 in Korean: "진설병" is the older church word, unknown to most readers, and the style guide says "빵", never "떡".

decisions.choice: "[읽지 못했느냐]" (L)
alternatives: ending the clause without a verb
decisions.reason: The Greek "how he entered ..." goes on with the question of 6:3; Korean needs the verb at the end of the clause, so Literal repeats it in brackets, as Mark 2:26 does in Korean.

source.text: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Κύριός ἐστιν τοῦ σαββάτου ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.

records.literal_gloss: And he was saying to them, Lord is of the Sabbath the Son of the Man.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying to them, "[The] Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath."
en.B: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told them, "The Son of Man is Lord over the Sabbath."
en.R: Then Jesus said to them, "The Son of Man is Lord over the Sabbath day."

es.L: Y les decía: «Señor del sábado es el Hijo del Hombre».
es.B: Y les dijo: «El Hijo del Hombre es Señor del sábado».
es.R: Luego Jesús les dijo: «El Hijo del Hombre es el Señor del sábado».

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur disait : « Le Fils de l’homme est Seigneur du sabbat. »
fr.B: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Le Fils de l’homme est le Seigneur du sabbat. »
fr.R: Puis Jésus leur a dit : « Le Fils de l’homme est Seigneur : {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a autorité sur le sabbat. »

sw.L: Naye alikuwa akiwaambia, "Bwana wa Sabato ni Mwana wa Adamu."
sw.B: Kisha aliwaambia, "Mwana wa Adamu ni Bwana wa Sabato."
sw.R: Kisha Yesu akawaambia, "Mwana wa Adamu ni Bwana wa siku ya Sabato."

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Con Người là Chúa của ngày Sa-bát."
vi.B: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Con Người là Chúa trên cả ngày Sa-bát."
vi.R: Rồi Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Con Người là Chúa, Đấng có quyền trên ngày Sa-bát."

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 그들에게 말씀하고 계셨다. "인자는 안식일의 주이다."
ko.B: 예수께서 또 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "인자는 안식일을 다스리는 주이다."
ko.R: 그리고 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "인자는 안식일을 다스리는 주인이다."

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus's name for himself, recalling Daniel 7:13-14
alternatives: a son of man: simply a human being
decisions.reason: In Hebrew "son of man" can mean a human being (Psalm 8:5). In Daniel 7:13-14 one like a son of man receives from God authority and a kingdom. Jesus uses the title of himself, as he did in 5:24.

decisions.choice: Lord of the Sabbath: the one with authority over the Sabbath
alternatives: one who simply keeps the Sabbath well
decisions.reason: God gave the Sabbath (Genesis 2:2-3; Exodus 20:8-11). To claim authority over it, to say what it is for and what is fitting on it, is a great claim. The word "Lord" stands first in the sentence for emphasis.

decisions.choice: this verse here, as in the SBLGNT
alternatives: the verse placed after 6:10, as in one ancient manuscript
decisions.reason: One ancient manuscript of the Gospels moves this saying after 6:10 and puts in its place a story, found nowhere else, about a man working on the Sabbath. Almost all manuscripts have the order of the SBLGNT. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Lord over the Sabbath (B, R); Lord of the Sabbath (L)
decisions.reason: "Over" makes clear that the title means authority.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker.

decisions.choice: Señor del sábado first (L)
decisions.reason: Spanish can put "Señor del sábado" first, as the Greek does for emphasis, and still read clearly, so Literal keeps the order the English cannot.

decisions.choice: el Hijo del Hombre
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: Jesus's name for himself (meaning decision m1), capitalised as a title.

decisions.choice: Seigneur du sabbat (L, B); est Seigneur : il a autorité sur le sabbat (R)
decisions.reason: French "Seigneur du sabbat" already says lordship over the day, so Literal and Balanced need no "over". Readable spells out the authority (m2), as the English Readable's "over" does; the "il" is the Son of Man, Jesus, and takes the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: Bwana wa Sabato first (L)
decisions.reason: Swahili can put "Bwana wa Sabato" first, as the Greek does for emphasis, so Literal keeps the order the English cannot.

decisions.choice: Mwana wa Adamu
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts, as in John: the settled Swahili title for Jesus's name for himself (meaning decision m1), never under the gender setting.

decisions.choice: "Con Người", capitalised, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The style guide's title for the Son of Man, as in Mark 2:28 and Luke 5:24.

decisions.choice: "인자" at every level; "주" (L, B), "주인" (R)
decisions.reason: As Mark 2:28 in Korean: Jesus speaks of himself, and a Korean speaker does not use the honorific "-님" of himself; Readable says "주인" (master). "인자" is the title used through the Gospels in Korean.

source.text: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ἑτέρῳ σαββάτῳ εἰσελθεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν καὶ διδάσκειν· καὶ ἦν ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖ καὶ ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ ἡ δεξιὰ ἦν ξηρά·

records.literal_gloss: It came about then on another Sabbath [that] to enter him into the synagogue and to teach; and there was a man there and the hand of him the right was withered;

en.L: And it happened on another Sabbath [that] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} entered into the synagogue and was teaching. And a man was there, and his right hand was withered.
en.B: Another Sabbath came, and Jesus went into the synagogue and taught there. A man was present whose right hand was withered.
en.R: On another Sabbath day Jesus went into the synagogue and taught the people. There was a man there whose right hand was weak and shrunken. He could not use it.

es.L: Y sucedió en otro sábado que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} entró en la sinagoga y enseñaba. Y había allí un hombre, y su mano derecha estaba seca.
es.B: Otro sábado, Jesús entró en la sinagoga y se puso a enseñar. Había allí un hombre que tenía la mano derecha atrofiada.
es.R: Otro sábado, Jesús entró en la sinagoga y enseñó a la gente. Había allí un hombre que tenía la mano derecha débil y encogida. No podía usarla.

fr.L: Et il arriva, un autre sabbat, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} entra dans la synagogue et y enseignait. Et il y avait là un homme, et sa main droite était desséchée.
fr.B: Un autre jour de sabbat, Jésus entra dans la synagogue et se mit à enseigner. Il s’y trouvait un homme dont la main droite était desséchée.
fr.R: Un autre jour de sabbat, Jésus est entré dans la synagogue et il a enseigné ceux qui étaient là. Il y avait un homme dont la main droite était paralysée et toute maigre. Il ne pouvait pas s’en servir.

sw.L: Ikawa katika Sabato nyingine aliingia ndani ya sinagogi, akawa akifundisha. Na palikuwa na mtu pale, na mkono wake wa kulia ulikuwa umekauka.
sw.B: Katika Sabato nyingine Yesu aliingia katika sinagogi, akafundisha. Palikuwa na mtu ambaye mkono wake wa kulia ulikuwa umesinyaa.
sw.R: Siku nyingine ya Sabato Yesu aliingia katika sinagogi, akawafundisha watu. Pale palikuwa na mtu ambaye mkono wake wa kulia ulikuwa dhaifu na umesinyaa. Hakuweza kuutumia.

vi.L: Và xảy ra là vào một ngày Sa-bát khác, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vào nhà hội và giảng dạy; và ở đó có một người, bàn tay phải của người ấy bị teo.
vi.B: Vào một ngày Sa-bát khác, Đức Giê-xu vào nhà hội và giảng dạy. Ở đó có một người bị teo bàn tay phải.
vi.R: Vào một ngày Sa-bát khác, Đức Giê-xu vào nhà hội và dạy dỗ dân chúng. Ở đó có một người bị tật ở bàn tay phải: bàn tay ấy khô teo, không cử động được.

ko.L: 또 다른 안식일에 [이런] 일이 있었다. 그분이 회당에 들어가셔서 가르치고 계셨는데, 거기에 한 사람이 있었고, 그의 오른손이 말라 있었다.
ko.B: 또 다른 안식일에 예수께서 회당에 들어가셔서 가르치셨다. 거기에 오른손이 오그라든 사람이 하나 있었다.
ko.R: 또 다른 안식일에 예수께서 회당에 들어가셔서 사람들을 가르치셨다. 거기에 오른손이 말라서 오그라든 사람이 있었다. 그는 그 손을 쓸 수 없었다.

decisions.choice: synagogue: the local meeting place where Jews gathered on the Sabbath for prayer and the reading and teaching of Scripture
decisions.reason: There was one temple, in Jerusalem, but a synagogue in every town. Jesus taught in them (4:15-16, 44).

decisions.choice: withered: dried up, shrunken and useless
decisions.reason: The word means dry. It describes a hand wasted or paralyzed, as in 1 Kings 13:4.

decisions.choice: his right hand: the hand used for work
decisions.reason: Only Luke says which hand it was. Losing the use of the right hand meant losing the ability to earn a living.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section.

decisions.choice: He could not use it.
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a withered hand meant for the man.

decisions.choice: seca (L); atrofiada (B); débil y encogida (R)
decisions.reason: The hand was dried up, shrunken and useless (meaning decision m2). "Seca" keeps the Greek picture, as in Matthew 12:10; "paralizada" would describe a different condition.

decisions.choice: umekauka (L); umesinyaa (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 12:10: the hand was dried up and shrunken (meaning decision m2). "Kukauka" keeps the Greek picture of drying; "kusinyaa" is to shrivel. "Kupooza" would describe paralysis, a different condition.

decisions.choice: "bị teo" (L, B); "bị tật ... khô teo, không cử động được" (R) for withered
decisions.reason: As in the parallel Mark 3:1: "teo" is the everyday word for a limb that has shrunk and lost its strength; Readable says what the condition was, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "말라 있었다" (L); "오그라든" (B); "말라서 오그라든" with "쓸 수 없었다" (R)
decisions.reason: As Mark 3:1 in Korean: Literal keeps the Greek word "dry", Balanced says what such a hand looks like, and Readable adds that it was useless, as the English Readable does.

source.text: παρετηροῦντο δὲ οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι εἰ ἐν τῷ σαββάτῳ θεραπεύει, ἵνα εὕρωσιν κατηγορεῖν αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Were watching closely then the scribes and the Pharisees whether on the Sabbath he heals, so that they might find to accuse him.

en.L: And the scribes and the Pharisees were watching closely [to see] whether {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would heal on the Sabbath, so that they might find [a way] to accuse {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: The scribes and the Pharisees kept a close watch on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to see whether {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would heal on the Sabbath, so that they could find a charge to bring against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: The teachers of the law and the Pharisees watched Jesus carefully. They wanted to see whether {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would heal anyone on the Sabbath day. Then they would have something to accuse {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} of.

es.L: Y los escribas y los fariseos observaban atentamente [para ver] si sanaba en sábado, a fin de encontrar [cómo] acusarlo.
es.B: Los escribas y los fariseos {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vigilaban de cerca para ver si sanaba en sábado, y así encontrar un motivo para acusarlo.
es.R: Los maestros de la ley y los fariseos vigilaban a Jesús con cuidado. Querían ver si sanaba a alguien en sábado. Así tendrían algo de qué acusarlo.

fr.L: Or les scribes et les Pharisiens observaient de près [pour voir] s’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} guérirait le jour du sabbat, afin de trouver [de quoi] {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}accuser.
fr.B: Les scribes et les Pharisiens {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} surveillaient de près pour voir s’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ferait une guérison le jour du sabbat ; ils voulaient trouver un motif d’accusation contre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Les spécialistes de la Loi et les Pharisiens surveillaient Jésus attentivement. Ils voulaient voir s’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} allait guérir quelqu’un le jour du sabbat. Comme cela, ils auraient une raison de {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}accuser.

sw.L: Na waandishi na Mafarisayo walikuwa wakimvizia [kuona] kama anaponya katika Sabato, ili wapate [njia ya] kumshtaki.
sw.B: Waandishi na Mafarisayo walikuwa wakimvizia ili waone kama angeponya siku ya Sabato, wapate sababu ya kumshtaki.
sw.R: Walimu wa sheria na Mafarisayo walikuwa wakimwangalia Yesu kwa makini. Walitaka kuona kama angemponya mtu siku ya Sabato. Ndipo wangepata jambo la kumshtaki.

vi.L: Và các thầy thông giáo và người Pha-ri-si rình xem {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} có chữa bệnh trong ngày Sa-bát không, để tìm [cớ] tố cáo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Các thầy thông giáo và người Pha-ri-si theo dõi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thật kỹ, xem {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} có chữa bệnh trong ngày Sa-bát không, để có cớ tố cáo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Các thầy dạy luật và người Pha-ri-si theo dõi Đức Giê-xu rất kỹ. Họ muốn xem {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} có chữa bệnh cho ai trong ngày Sa-bát không. Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chữa, họ sẽ có cớ để tố cáo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 율법학자들과 바리새파 사람들은 그분이 안식일에 [병을] 고치시는지 [보려고] 그분을 지켜보고 있었다. 그분을 고발할 [거리를] 찾으려는 것이었다.
ko.B: 율법학자들과 바리새파 사람들은 예수께서 안식일에 병을 고치시는지 보려고 예수를 눈여겨 지켜보았다. 예수를 고발할 구실을 찾으려는 것이었다.
ko.R: 율법 선생들과 바리새파 사람들은 예수를 유심히 지켜보았다. 예수께서 안식일에 누구의 병이든 고쳐 주시는지 보려는 것이었다. 그렇게 하시면 예수를 고발할 생각이었다.

decisions.choice: scribes: experts who taught and explained the law of Moses
decisions.reason: The word means men of letters, but in the Gospels the scribes are teachers of the law. Many of them were Pharisees (5:21, 30).

decisions.choice: heal on the Sabbath: counted by many as work, unless a life was in danger
alternatives: clearly forbidden in the law of Moses
decisions.reason: The law of Moses does not mention healing on the Sabbath. Later Jewish teaching allowed help on the Sabbath when a life was in danger, but this man's hand could have waited a day (compare 13:14).

decisions.choice: were watching closely: watching for a chance to catch him
decisions.reason: The verb means to watch carefully, often with hostile intent (14:1; 20:20).

decisions.choice: teachers of the law
decisions.reason: "Scribes" today suggests people who copy documents. Readable says what they did.

decisions.choice: [a way] (L); a charge (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek says only that they might find to accuse him; something to accuse him with is meant.

decisions.choice: los escribas (L, B); los maestros de la ley (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: "escribas" names the group; Readable says what they did, as the English Readable says "teachers of the law" (meaning decision m1). The same in 6:11.

decisions.choice: les scribes (L, B); les spécialistes de la Loi (R)
alternatives: les maîtres de la Loi at every level
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms: Literal and Balanced keep the traditional title, and Readable says what they did, as the English Readable's "teachers of the law" does (m1).

decisions.choice: waandishi (L, B); walimu wa sheria (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: "waandishi" names the group; Readable says what they did, as the English Readable says "teachers of the law" (meaning decision m1). The same in 6:11.

decisions.choice: wakimvizia
decisions.reason: The Greek is watching closely for a chance to catch him (meaning decision m3). "Kuvizia" is to watch someone in order to catch them out, where "kutazama" is only to look.

decisions.choice: "thầy thông giáo" (L, B); "thầy dạy luật" (R) for the scribes (whole chapter)
decisions.reason: The settled terms for the Gospels, as in Mark 1:22 and Luke 5:21.

decisions.choice: "rình xem" (L); "theo dõi thật kỹ" (B)
decisions.reason: As in the parallel Mark 3:2: the verb is watching in order to catch a fault; "rình" says so by itself, and Balanced lets "để có cớ tố cáo" show the motive.

decisions.choice: "율법학자들" (L, B); "율법 선생들" (R) for the scribes
decisions.reason: The terms settled for the Gospels in Korean, as in Luke 5:21 and Mark 3:22.
Korean needs an object for "heal", a verb of seeing before the "whether" clause, and a noun for "find to accuse"; Literal brackets them, as Mark 3:2 does in Korean.

source.text: αὐτὸς δὲ ᾔδει τοὺς διαλογισμοὺς αὐτῶν, εἶπεν δὲ τῷ ἀνδρὶ τῷ ξηρὰν ἔχοντι τὴν χεῖρα· Ἔγειρε καὶ στῆθι εἰς τὸ μέσον· καὶ ἀναστὰς ἔστη.

records.literal_gloss: He but knew the thoughts of them, said and to the man the withered having the hand, Rise and stand into the middle; and having risen he stood.

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} knew their thoughts, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to the man who had the withered hand, "Get up and stand in the middle." And rising, he stood [there].
en.B: He knew their thoughts, though, and said to the man with the withered hand, "Get up and come stand in the middle." The man rose and stood there.
en.R: But Jesus knew what was in their minds. He said to the man with the weak hand, "Get up and stand here where everyone can see you." So the man got up and stood there.

es.L: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} conocía los pensamientos de ellos, y dijo al hombre que tenía la mano seca: «Levántate y ponte en medio». Y él, levantándose, se quedó de pie [allí].
es.B: Él, sin embargo, conocía lo que pensaban, y le dijo al hombre de la mano atrofiada: «Levántate y ponte aquí en medio». El hombre se levantó y se quedó allí de pie.
es.R: Pero Jesús sabía lo que estaban pensando. Le dijo al hombre de la mano débil: «Levántate y ponte aquí, donde todos te vean». Así que el hombre se levantó y se quedó allí de pie.

fr.L: Mais {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} connaissait leurs pensées, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit à l’homme qui avait la main desséchée : « Lève-toi et tiens-toi au milieu. » Et, s’étant levé, il se tint [là].
fr.B: Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} connaissait leurs pensées, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit à l’homme à la main desséchée : « Lève-toi, et viens te placer au milieu. » L’homme se leva et resta debout.
fr.R: Mais Jésus savait ce qu’ils pensaient. Il a dit à l’homme à la main malade : « Lève-toi et mets-toi ici, où tout le monde peut te voir. » Alors l’homme s’est levé et il est resté là, debout.

sw.L: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} aliyajua mawazo yao, akamwambia yule mtu aliyekuwa na mkono uliokauka, "Inuka, usimame katikati." Naye akainuka, akasimama [pale].
sw.B: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} aliyajua mawazo yao, akamwambia yule mtu mwenye mkono uliosinyaa, "Simama, uje hapa katikati." Yule mtu akainuka, akasimama pale.
sw.R: Lakini Yesu alijua walichokuwa wakifikiri. Akamwambia yule mtu mwenye mkono dhaifu, "Inuka, usimame hapa ambapo kila mtu anaweza kukuona." Basi yule mtu akainuka, akasimama pale.

vi.L: Nhưng chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} biết những ý nghĩ của họ, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với người có bàn tay bị teo: "Hãy đứng dậy và đứng ra giữa." Và người ấy đứng dậy và đứng [đó].
vi.B: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} biết rõ ý nghĩ của họ, nên {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bảo người bị teo tay: "Hãy đứng dậy, ra đứng giữa đây." Người ấy đứng dậy và ra đứng đó.
vi.R: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu biết họ đang nghĩ gì trong lòng. Ngài bảo người bị tật ở tay: "Hãy đứng dậy, ra đứng ở đây cho mọi người cùng thấy." Người ấy đứng dậy và ra đứng đó.

ko.L: 그러나 그분은 그들의 생각을 알고 계셨다. 그래서 손이 마른 그 사람에게 말씀하셨다. "일어나서 한가운데에 서라." 그러자 그가 일어나 [거기에] 섰다.
ko.B: 그러나 예수께서는 그들의 생각을 아시고, 손이 오그라든 사람에게 말씀하셨다. "일어나서 이 가운데로 나와 서라." 그 사람은 일어나 그 자리에 섰다.
ko.R: 그러나 예수께서는 그들이 속으로 무슨 생각을 하는지 아셨다. 예수께서 손이 오그라든 사람에게 말씀하셨다. "일어나서 모든 사람이 볼 수 있게 여기 앞에 서라." 그러자 그 사람이 일어나서 거기에 섰다.

decisions.choice: he knew their thoughts: he knew what they were reasoning in secret
decisions.reason: Luke shows Jesus knowing hidden thoughts (5:22; 9:47), as Simeon said the thoughts of many hearts would be revealed (2:35).

decisions.choice: stand in the middle: where everyone in the synagogue could see
decisions.reason: Jesus does not heal in secret. He puts the question of 6:9 before them all.

decisions.choice: the man
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear who stood up.

decisions.choice: here where everyone can see you
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means.

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς πρὸς αὐτούς· Ἐπερωτῶ ὑμᾶς, εἰ ἔξεστιν τῷ σαββάτῳ ἀγαθοποιῆσαι ἢ κακοποιῆσαι, ψυχὴν σῶσαι ἢ ἀπολέσαι;

records.literal_gloss: Said then Jesus to them, I ask you whether it is lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil, life to save or to destroy?

en.L: Then Jesus said to them, "I ask you, is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil, to save a life or to destroy [it]?"
en.B: Then Jesus said to them, "Let {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} put a question to you: on the Sabbath, does the law allow doing good, or doing harm? Saving a life, or destroying it?"
en.R: Then Jesus said to them, "I want to ask you something. On the Sabbath day, does the law let us do good, or do harm? Does it let us save a life, or destroy it?"

es.L: Entonces Jesús les dijo: «{{plural_you:Les|Os}} pregunto: ¿es lícito en sábado hacer el bien o hacer el mal, salvar una vida o destruirla?».
es.B: Entonces Jesús les dijo: «{{plural_you:Permítanme|Permitidme}} {{plural_you:hacerles|haceros}} una pregunta: en sábado, ¿permite la ley hacer el bien o hacer daño? ¿Salvar una vida o destruirla?».
es.R: Entonces Jesús les dijo: «Quiero {{plural_you:preguntarles|preguntaros}} algo. En sábado, ¿nos permite la ley hacer el bien o hacer daño? ¿Nos permite salvar una vida o destruirla?».

fr.L: Puis Jésus leur dit : « Je vous demande : est-il permis, le jour du sabbat, de faire du bien ou de faire du mal, de sauver une vie ou de [la] détruire ? »
fr.B: Jésus leur dit alors : « J’ai une question à vous poser : le jour du sabbat, la Loi permet-elle de faire du bien, ou de faire du tort ? De sauver une vie, ou de la détruire ? »
fr.R: Ensuite, Jésus leur a dit : « Je veux vous demander quelque chose. Le jour du sabbat, est-ce que la Loi nous permet de faire du bien, ou de faire du mal ? Est-ce qu’elle nous permet de sauver une vie, ou de la détruire ? »

sw.L: Kisha Yesu akawaambia, "Nawauliza, je, ni halali katika Sabato kutenda mema au kutenda mabaya, kuokoa uhai au kuuangamiza?"
sw.B: Kisha Yesu akawaambia, "Niwaulize swali: je, siku ya Sabato sheria inaruhusu kutenda mema au kutenda mabaya? Kuokoa uhai au kuuangamiza?"
sw.R: Kisha Yesu akawaambia, "Nataka kuwauliza jambo moja. Siku ya Sabato, je, sheria inaturuhusu kutenda mema au kutenda mabaya? Je, inaturuhusu kuokoa uhai wa mtu au kuuangamiza?"

vi.L: Và Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Ta hỏi các người, trong ngày Sa-bát, được phép làm điều lành hay làm điều dữ, cứu một mạng người hay hủy diệt [nó]?"
vi.B: Rồi Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Ta hỏi các người: trong ngày Sa-bát, luật pháp cho phép làm điều tốt hay làm điều hại, cứu mạng người hay hủy hoại mạng người?"
vi.R: Rồi Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Ta muốn hỏi các người một điều. Trong ngày Sa-bát, luật pháp cho chúng ta làm điều tốt hay làm điều hại? Luật pháp cho chúng ta cứu mạng người hay hủy hoại mạng người?"

ko.L: 그리고 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "내가 너희에게 묻는다. 안식일에 선을 행하는 것과 악을 행하는 것, 목숨을 구하는 것과 멸하는 것 가운데 어느 것이 허락되어 있느냐?"
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "내가 너희에게 하나 묻겠다. 안식일에 율법이 허락하는 것이 선한 일을 하는 것이냐, 해를 끼치는 것이냐? 목숨을 살리는 것이냐, 없애는 것이냐?"
ko.R: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "너희에게 묻겠다. 안식일에 율법은 우리에게 좋은 일을 하라고 하느냐, 나쁜 일을 하라고 하느냐? 사람의 목숨을 살리라고 하느냐, 죽게 하라고 하느냐?"

decisions.choice: life: a person's life
decisions.reason: The word can mean the soul, but beside "save" and "destroy" it means a person's life, as often (9:24; 12:22).

decisions.choice: do good or do harm: refusing to do good when one can is itself a kind of harm
alternatives: a choice only between healing and killing
decisions.reason: Jesus does not allow a middle way. While he plans to do good, his opponents are planning harm against him on the same Sabbath (6:7, 11).

decisions.choice: do evil: do harm
decisions.reason: The verb is the opposite of "do good" and means to harm someone.

decisions.choice: doing harm (B); do harm (R)
decisions.reason: As the meaning decision explains, the contrast is between helping and harming.

decisions.choice: does the law let us
decisions.reason: Readable puts the question in plain words.

decisions.choice: faire du mal (L, R); faire du tort (B)
decisions.reason: "Faire le mal" would mean doing moral evil in general; the contrast is between helping and harming someone (m3), which French says with "faire du mal" and, in Balanced, "faire du tort".

decisions.choice: uhai
decisions.reason: The word here is a person's life (meaning decision m1). "Uhai" is being alive, the life that can be saved or lost; "maisha" is a lifetime or way of living, and "nafsi" would suggest the soul.

decisions.choice: "mạng người" for the life that can be saved or destroyed
decisions.reason: As in the parallel Mark 3:4: the word here means a person's life (meaning decision); "linh hồn" (soul) would mislead, and "sự sống" is kept for zoe.

decisions.choice: "목숨" for psychē (life)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 3:4 and the Korean John, "목숨" is the life a person has and can lose; "생명" is kept for zōē.

source.text: καὶ περιβλεψάμενος πάντας αὐτοὺς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἔκτεινον τὴν χεῖρά σου· ὁ δὲ ἐποίησεν, καὶ ἀπεκατεστάθη ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And having looked around at all them he said to him, Stretch out the hand of you. He then did, and was restored the hand of him.

en.L: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had looked around at all of them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him, "Stretch out your hand." He did [it], and his hand was restored.
en.B: Jesus looked around at every one of them. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to the man, "Hold out your hand." The man did, and his hand was made healthy again.
en.R: Jesus looked around at all of them. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to the man, "Hold out your hand." The man held it out, and his hand was healed. It was normal again.

es.L: Y después de mirarlos a todos alrededor, le dijo: «Extiende tu mano». Él lo hizo, y su mano fue restaurada.
es.B: Jesús miró a su alrededor, a cada uno de ellos, y luego le dijo al hombre: «Extiende la mano». El hombre lo hizo, y su mano quedó sana otra vez.
es.R: Jesús los miró a todos. Luego le dijo al hombre: «Extiende la mano». El hombre la extendió, y su mano quedó sana. Estaba normal otra vez.

fr.L: Et, les ayant tous regardés à la ronde, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui dit : « Étends ta main. » Il le fit, et sa main fut rétablie.
fr.B: Jésus les regarda tous, l’un après l’autre, puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit à l’homme : « Tends la main. » L’homme le fit, et sa main redevint saine.
fr.R: Jésus les a tous regardés. Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a dit à l’homme : « Tends la main. » L’homme l’a tendue, et sa main a été guérie. Elle était de nouveau normale.

sw.L: Na akiisha kuwatazama wote pande zote, akamwambia, "Nyoosha mkono wako." Naye akafanya hivyo, na mkono wake ukarejeshwa.
sw.B: Yesu aliwatazama wote waliokuwa pale, kisha akamwambia yule mtu, "Nyoosha mkono wako." Akafanya hivyo, na mkono wake ukawa mzima tena.
sw.R: Yesu aliwatazama wote waliokuwa karibu naye. Kisha akamwambia yule mtu, "Nyoosha mkono wako." Yule mtu akaunyoosha, na mkono wake ukapona. Ukawa sawa tena.

vi.L: Và nhìn quanh tất cả bọn họ, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với người ấy: "Hãy giơ tay của anh ra." Người ấy làm [vậy], và tay người ấy được phục hồi.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nhìn quanh hết thảy mọi người, rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bảo người ấy: "Hãy giơ tay ra." Người ấy làm theo, và tay người ấy được lành lại như trước.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nhìn quanh tất cả bọn họ. Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bảo người ấy: "Hãy giơ tay ra." Người ấy giơ tay ra, và bàn tay được chữa lành. Nó lại lành lặn như trước.

ko.L: 그리고 그분은 그들 모두를 둘러보시고 그에게 말씀하셨다. "네 손을 내밀어라." 그가 [그렇게] 하자, 그의 손이 회복되었다.
ko.B: 예수께서 그들을 모두 둘러보신 뒤에 그 사람에게 말씀하셨다. "손을 내밀어라." 그 사람이 그렇게 하자, 손이 다시 성하게 되었다.
ko.R: 예수께서 그곳에 있는 사람들을 모두 둘러보셨다. 그리고 그 사람에게 말씀하셨다. "손을 내밀어라." 그 사람이 손을 내밀자 손이 나았다. 손이 전과 똑같이 멀쩡해졌다.

decisions.choice: his hand was restored: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: his hand was restored, as healthy as the other, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "as healthy as the other", words found in Matthew 12:13. Early manuscripts lack them. The healing is complete either way. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: restored: brought back to its former healthy state
decisions.reason: The verb means to put back as it was.

decisions.choice: the man
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear whom Jesus spoke to.

decisions.choice: "anh" for the man in Jesus' command (L)
decisions.reason: The ordinary respectful word for a grown man, as Jesus uses it to the healed man in 5:14; Balanced and Readable leave the possessive out, as Vietnamese naturally does.

source.text: αὐτοὶ δὲ ἐπλήσθησαν ἀνοίας, καὶ διελάλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους τί ἂν ποιήσαιεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: They then were filled with fury, and were discussing with one another what they might do to the Jesus.

en.L: But they were filled with senseless rage, and they were talking over with one another what they might do to Jesus.
en.B: This filled them with mindless rage, and they talked together about what they could do to Jesus.
en.R: But the teachers of the law and the Pharisees became wildly angry. They started talking with each other about what they could do to Jesus.

es.L: Pero ellos se llenaron de furia insensata, y discutían unos con otros qué podrían hacerle a Jesús.
es.B: Ellos se llenaron de una rabia ciega, y hablaban entre sí sobre qué podrían hacer con Jesús.
es.R: Pero los maestros de la ley y los fariseos se enfurecieron muchísimo. Comenzaron a hablar entre ellos sobre qué podían hacerle a Jesús.

fr.L: Mais eux furent remplis d’une fureur insensée, et ils discutaient entre eux de ce qu’ils pourraient faire à Jésus.
fr.B: Ils en devinrent fous de rage, et ils se demandèrent ensemble ce qu’ils pourraient bien faire à Jésus.
fr.R: Mais les spécialistes de la Loi et les Pharisiens se sont mis dans une colère folle. Ils ont commencé à discuter entre eux de ce qu’ils pourraient faire contre Jésus.

sw.L: Lakini wao walijawa na ghadhabu isiyo na akili, wakawa wakijadiliana wao kwa wao ni nini wangemfanyia Yesu.
sw.B: Lakini wao walijawa na hasira kali isiyo na busara, wakashauriana wao kwa wao ni nini wangemtendea Yesu.
sw.R: Lakini walimu wa sheria na Mafarisayo walikasirika sana. Wakaanza kuzungumza wao kwa wao kuhusu jambo ambalo wangemfanyia Yesu.

vi.L: Nhưng họ đầy dẫy cơn giận điên cuồng, và bàn với nhau xem họ có thể làm gì Đức Giê-xu.
vi.B: Họ giận dữ đến mất cả lý trí, và bàn tính với nhau xem có thể làm gì Đức Giê-xu.
vi.R: Nhưng các thầy dạy luật và người Pha-ri-si vô cùng tức giận. Họ bắt đầu bàn với nhau xem phải làm gì với Đức Giê-xu.

ko.L: 그러나 그들은 분별을 잃은 분노로 가득 찼다. 그리고 예수를 어떻게 할지 서로 의논하고 있었다.
ko.B: 그들은 몹시 화가 나서 제정신을 잃었다. 그리고 예수를 어떻게 할지 서로 의논하였다.
ko.R: 율법 선생들과 바리새파 사람들은 몹시 화가 났다. 그들은 예수를 어떻게 하면 좋을지 서로 이야기하기 시작했다.

decisions.choice: fury: rage that has lost all good sense
decisions.reason: The word means mindlessness. Here it is a fury so great that they cannot think clearly.

decisions.choice: what they might do: they are uncertain what to do
decisions.reason: The verb form expresses doubt. Luke does not yet speak of a plot to kill him, as Mark 3:6 does.

decisions.choice: the teachers of the law and the Pharisees
decisions.reason: Readable names who they were (6:7).

decisions.choice: furia insensata (L); rabia ciega (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is rage that has lost all good sense (meaning decision m1). Plain "ira" or "enojo" would lose the senselessness, so each level adds a word for it.

decisions.choice: "cơn giận điên cuồng" (L); "giận dữ đến mất cả lý trí" (B)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision gives rage that has lost all good sense; Vietnamese says both the anger and the loss of reason, where "điên dại" alone would sound like madness.

decisions.choice: "분별을 잃은 분노" (L); "몹시 화가 나서 제정신을 잃었다" (B); "몹시 화가 났다" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is rage that has lost all good sense (meaning decision); Korean says both the anger and the loss of sense at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις ἐξελθεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ ὄρος προσεύξασθαι, καὶ ἦν διανυκτερεύων ἐν τῇ προσευχῇ τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: It came about then in the days these [that] to go out him to the mountain to pray, and he was spending the night in the prayer of the God.

en.L: And it happened in these days [that] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out to the mountain to pray, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was spending the whole night in prayer to God.
en.B: During those days Jesus went off to the mountain to pray, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stayed up all night in prayer to God.
en.R: About that time, Jesus went up on a mountain to pray. He prayed to God all through the night.

es.L: Y sucedió en estos días que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} salió al monte a orar, y pasaba toda la noche en oración a Dios.
es.B: Por aquellos días, Jesús se fue al monte a orar, y pasó toda la noche orando a Dios.
es.R: Por ese tiempo, Jesús subió a un monte para orar. Estuvo orando a Dios toda la noche.

fr.L: Or il arriva en ces jours-là qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sortit vers la montagne pour prier, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} passait toute la nuit en prière à Dieu.
fr.B: En ces jours-là, Jésus s’en alla sur la montagne pour prier, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} passa toute la nuit à prier Dieu.
fr.R: À cette époque, Jésus est monté sur une montagne pour prier. Il a prié Dieu toute la nuit.

sw.L: Ikawa katika siku hizo alitoka akaenda mlimani kuomba, naye akakesha usiku kucha katika maombi kwa Mungu.
sw.B: Siku hizo Yesu alikwenda mlimani kuomba, akakesha usiku mzima akimwomba Mungu.
sw.R: Wakati huo Yesu alipanda mlimani kuomba. Akamwomba Mungu usiku wote.

vi.L: Và xảy ra là trong những ngày ấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi lên núi để cầu nguyện, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thức suốt đêm cầu nguyện với Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Trong những ngày ấy, Đức Giê-xu lên núi cầu nguyện, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thức suốt đêm cầu nguyện với Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Vào khoảng thời gian đó, Đức Giê-xu lên một ngọn núi để cầu nguyện. Ngài cầu nguyện với Đức Chúa Trời suốt cả đêm.

ko.L: 그 날들에 [이런] 일이 있었다. 그분이 기도하시려고 산으로 나가셨는데, 하나님께 드리는 기도로 밤을 지새우고 계셨다.
ko.B: 그 무렵에 예수께서 기도하시려고 산으로 가셨다. 그리고 밤새도록 하나님께 기도하셨다.
ko.R: 그 무렵 예수께서 기도하시려고 산에 올라가셨다. 예수께서는 밤새도록 하나님께 기도하셨다.

decisions.choice: the prayer of God: prayer to God
alternatives: a place of prayer belonging to God
decisions.reason: The phrase names the one to whom the prayer is made.

decisions.choice: Jesus prays before the choice of the twelve
decisions.reason: Luke shows Jesus praying at the great moments of his work (3:21; 9:18, 28-29; 22:41-44). Here it comes before he chooses the twelve.

decisions.choice: the mountain: the hill country
decisions.reason: The article may point to the hills near the Sea of Galilee rather than a named mountain.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section.

decisions.choice: "cầu nguyện với Đức Chúa Trời" for "the prayer of God"
alternatives: "lời cầu nguyện của Đức Chúa Trời"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says prayer to God; a literal "of God" would make God the one praying, so even Literal says "với".

decisions.choice: "하나님께 드리는 기도" (L) for "the prayer of God"
decisions.reason: The genitive means prayer to God (meaning decision); "하나님의 기도" would read as God's own prayer.

source.text: καὶ ὅτε ἐγένετο ἡμέρα, προσεφώνησεν τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐκλεξάμενος ἀπ’ αὐτῶν δώδεκα, οὓς καὶ ἀποστόλους ὠνόμασεν, Σίμωνα ὃν καὶ ὠνόμασεν Πέτρον καὶ Ἀνδρέαν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην καὶ Φίλιππον καὶ Βαρθολομαῖον καὶ Μαθθαῖον καὶ Θωμᾶν καὶ Ἰάκωβον Ἁλφαίου καὶ Σίμωνα τὸν καλούμενον Ζηλωτὴν καὶ Ἰούδαν Ἰακώβου καὶ Ἰούδαν Ἰσκαριὼθ ὃς ἐγένετο προδότης.

records.literal_gloss: And when it became day, he called to [him] the disciples of him, and having chosen from them twelve, whom also apostles he named, \v 14 Simon whom also he named Peter, and Andrew the brother of him, and James and John and Philip and Bartholomew \v 15 and Matthew and Thomas and James [son] of Alphaeus and Simon the [one] called Zealot \v 16 and Judas [son] of James and Judas Iscariot, who became betrayer.

en.L: And when day came, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples to [{{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}], and choosing twelve from them, whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also named apostles: \v 14 Simon, whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also named Peter, and Andrew his brother, and James and John and Philip and Bartholomew \v 15 and Matthew and Thomas and James [son] of Alphaeus and Simon who was called [the] Zealot \v 16 and Judas [son] of James and Judas Iscariot, who became [a] betrayer.
en.B: At daybreak {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} summoned {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples and picked out twelve of them, giving them the name apostles. \v 14 They were Simon, to whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave the name Peter, and Simon's brother Andrew; James and John; Philip and Bartholomew; \v 15 Matthew and Thomas; James son of Alphaeus, and Simon, known as the Zealot; \v 16 Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, the one who turned traitor.
en.R: In the morning, Jesus called {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples to come to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. From them {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose twelve men, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called them apostles, which means people who are sent out. \v 14 These were the twelve: Simon, whom Jesus also named Peter, and Simon's brother Andrew; James and John; Philip and Bartholomew; \v 15 Matthew and Thomas; James, the son of Alphaeus; Simon, who was called the Zealot; \v 16 Judas, the son of James; and Judas Iscariot, who later became a traitor.

es.L: Y cuando se hizo de día, llamó a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos, y escogiendo de entre ellos a doce, a los que también nombró apóstoles: \v 14 Simón, a quien también nombró Pedro, y Andrés su hermano, y Santiago y Juan y Felipe y Bartolomé \v 15 y Mateo y Tomás y Santiago [hijo] de Alfeo y Simón, el llamado Zelote, \v 16 y Judas [hijo] de Santiago y Judas Iscariote, que llegó a ser traidor.
es.B: Al amanecer, reunió a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos y escogió a doce de ellos, a quienes dio el nombre de apóstoles. \v 14 Eran Simón, a quien {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} puso el nombre de Pedro, y Andrés, hermano de Simón; Santiago y Juan; Felipe y Bartolomé; \v 15 Mateo y Tomás; Santiago, hijo de Alfeo, y Simón, conocido como el Zelote; \v 16 Judas, hijo de Santiago, y Judas Iscariote, el que se volvió traidor.
es.R: Por la mañana, Jesús llamó a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos para que vinieran a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. De entre ellos escogió a doce hombres, y los llamó apóstoles, que significa personas enviadas. \v 14 Estos eran los doce: Simón, a quien Jesús también llamó Pedro, y su hermano Andrés; Santiago y Juan; Felipe y Bartolomé; \v 15 Mateo y Tomás; Santiago, hijo de Alfeo; Simón, al que llamaban el Zelote; \v 16 Judas, hijo de Santiago, y Judas Iscariote, que después se convirtió en traidor.

fr.L: Et quand le jour vint, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} appela {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples [auprès de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}], et, ayant choisi parmi eux douze, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nomma aussi apôtres : \v 14 Simon, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nomma aussi Pierre, et André son frère, et Jacques et Jean, et Philippe et Barthélemy, \v 15 et Matthieu et Thomas, et Jacques [fils] d’Alphée, et Simon appelé [le] Zélote, \v 16 et Judas [fils] de Jacques, et Judas Iscariot, qui devint traître.
fr.B: Au lever du jour, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} appela {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples et en choisit douze parmi eux, à qui {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} donna le nom d’apôtres. \v 14 C’étaient Simon, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nomma Pierre, et André, le frère de Simon ; Jacques et Jean ; Philippe et Barthélemy ; \v 15 Matthieu et Thomas ; Jacques, fils d’Alphée, et Simon, qu’on appelait le Zélote ; \v 16 Jude, fils de Jacques, et Judas Iscariot, celui qui devint un traître.
fr.R: Le matin, Jésus a appelé {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples pour qu’ils viennent près de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Parmi eux, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a choisi douze hommes, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les a appelés apôtres, un mot qui veut dire « envoyés ». \v 14 Voici ces douze hommes : Simon, que Jésus a aussi appelé Pierre, et André, le frère de Simon ; Jacques et Jean ; Philippe et Barthélemy ; \v 15 Matthieu et Thomas ; Jacques, le fils d’Alphée ; Simon, qu’on appelait le Zélote ; \v 16 Jude, le fils de Jacques ; et Judas Iscariot, qui plus tard est devenu un traître.

sw.L: Na kulipokucha, aliwaita wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} [waje {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}], na akichagua kumi na wawili kati yao, ambao pia aliwaita mitume: \v 14 Simoni, ambaye pia alimwita Petro, na Andrea ndugu yake, na Yakobo na Yohana na Filipo na Bartholomayo \v 15 na Mathayo na Tomaso na Yakobo [mwana] wa Alfayo na Simoni aitwaye Mzelote \v 16 na Yuda [mwana] wa Yakobo na Yuda Iskariote, aliyekuja kuwa msaliti.
sw.B: Kulipopambazuka, aliwaita wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, akachagua kumi na wawili kati yao, akawapa jina mitume. \v 14 Hao walikuwa Simoni, ambaye alimpa jina Petro, na Andrea ndugu yake Simoni; Yakobo na Yohana; Filipo na Bartholomayo; \v 15 Mathayo na Tomaso; Yakobo mwana wa Alfayo, na Simoni aliyejulikana kama Mzelote; \v 16 Yuda mwana wa Yakobo, na Yuda Iskariote, yule aliyegeuka kuwa msaliti.
sw.R: Asubuhi Yesu aliwaita wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} waje {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}. Kati yao akachagua watu kumi na wawili, akawaita mitume, yaani watu wanaotumwa. \v 14 Hawa ndio wale kumi na wawili: Simoni, ambaye Yesu alimpa pia jina Petro, na Andrea ndugu yake Simoni; Yakobo na Yohana; Filipo na Bartholomayo; \v 15 Mathayo na Tomaso; Yakobo mwana wa Alfayo; Simoni, aliyeitwa Mzelote; \v 16 Yuda mwana wa Yakobo; na Yuda Iskariote, ambaye baadaye alikuja kuwa msaliti.

vi.L: Và khi trời sáng, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} gọi các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến, và chọn trong số họ mười hai [người], là những người {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cũng gọi là sứ đồ: \v 14 Si-môn, là người {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cũng đặt tên là Phi-e-rơ, và Anh-rê, anh em của ông, và Gia-cơ và Giăng và Phi-líp và Ba-thê-lê-my \v 15 và Ma-thi-ơ và Thô-ma và Gia-cơ [con] của A-phê và Si-môn được gọi là Xê-lốt \v 16 và Giu-đa [con] của Gia-cơ và Giu-đa Ích-ca-ri-ốt, là người đã trở thành kẻ phản bội.
vi.B: Khi trời sáng, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} gọi các môn đồ đến và chọn ra mười hai người trong số họ, đặt tên cho họ là sứ đồ. \v 14 Đó là Si-môn, người {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đặt tên là Phi-e-rơ, và Anh-rê, anh em của Si-môn; Gia-cơ và Giăng; Phi-líp và Ba-thê-lê-my; \v 15 Ma-thi-ơ và Thô-ma; Gia-cơ con A-phê, và Si-môn, người được gọi là Xê-lốt; \v 16 Giu-đa con Gia-cơ, và Giu-đa Ích-ca-ri-ốt, người đã trở thành kẻ phản bội.
vi.R: Sáng hôm sau, Đức Giê-xu gọi các môn đồ đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Trong số họ, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chọn mười hai người và gọi họ là sứ đồ, nghĩa là những người được sai đi. \v 14 Mười hai người đó là: Si-môn, người được Đức Giê-xu đặt thêm tên là Phi-e-rơ, và Anh-rê, anh em của Si-môn; Gia-cơ và Giăng; Phi-líp và Ba-thê-lê-my; \v 15 Ma-thi-ơ và Thô-ma; Gia-cơ con của A-phê; Si-môn, người được gọi là "người Nhiệt Thành"; \v 16 Giu-đa con của Gia-cơ; và Giu-đa Ích-ca-ri-ốt, người về sau đã phản bội {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그리고 날이 밝자, 그분은 그분의 제자들을 불러 모으시고, 그들 가운데서 열둘을 택하셨다. 그분은 그들을 사도라고도 부르셨다. \v 14 [그들은] 그분이 베드로라고도 이름 지어 주신 시몬과 그의 형제 안드레, 그리고 야고보와 요한과 빌립과 바돌로매와 \v 15 마태와 도마와 알패오의 [아들] 야고보와 열심당원이라 불리는 시몬과 \v 16 야고보의 [아들] 유다와, 배반자가 된 가룟 유다이다.
ko.B: 날이 밝자 예수께서 제자들을 부르시고, 그들 가운데서 열두 사람을 뽑으셔서 사도라고 부르셨다. \v 14 그들은 예수께서 베드로라는 이름을 지어 주신 시몬과 그의 형제 안드레, 야고보와 요한, 빌립과 바돌로매, \v 15 마태와 도마, 알패오의 아들 야고보와 열심당원이라고 불리는 시몬, \v 16 야고보의 아들 유다와, 나중에 배반자가 된 가룟 유다이다.
ko.R: 아침이 되자 예수께서 제자들을 부르셨다. 그리고 그들 가운데서 열두 사람을 뽑으셔서 사도라고 부르셨다. 사도는 보냄을 받은 사람이라는 뜻이다. \v 14 그 열두 사람은 이렇다. 예수께서 베드로라는 이름도 지어 주신 시몬과 그의 형제 안드레, 야고보와 요한, 빌립과 바돌로매, \v 15 마태와 도마, 알패오의 아들 야고보, 열심당원이라고 불리던 시몬, \v 16 야고보의 아들 유다, 그리고 나중에 배반자가 된 가룟 유다였다.

decisions.choice: apostles: men sent out as messengers, with the authority of the one who sends them
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "to send out". Jesus will send the twelve out to preach and heal (9:1-2, 10). Luke often calls the twelve "the apostles" (17:5; 22:14; Acts 1:26).

decisions.choice: twelve: as many as the tribes of Israel
decisions.reason: Jesus gathers God's people anew around twelve leaders, as Israel had twelve tribes (22:30).

decisions.choice: Peter: a name meaning rock
decisions.reason: Jesus gave Simon the name. John 1:42 gives its Aramaic form, Cephas.

decisions.choice: the Zealot: either a man zealous for God's law, or one who had belonged to those who wanted to drive out Rome by force
alternatives: a member of the later Zealot party only
decisions.reason: The word means one full of zeal. The party called the Zealots took that name in the war against Rome in AD 66-70, but men of that kind were active before. Either way the name describes Simon's past or his character, and Jesus chose him with Matthew, who had collected taxes for Rome's rulers.

decisions.choice: Judas of James: Judas son of James
decisions.reason: The Greek gives only the name of a relative, which usually means the father. Jude 1 speaks of a Judas the brother of James, which led some to read "brother" here. Matthew 10:3 and Mark 3:18 have Thaddaeus in this place, probably another name for the same man.

decisions.choice: Iscariot: probably "man of Kerioth", a town in Judea
alternatives: a word meaning assassin or false one
decisions.reason: Kerioth is named in Joshua 15:25. Other explanations have been offered, and none is certain.

decisions.choice: betrayer: one who hands someone over to enemies
decisions.reason: Luke looks ahead to 22:3-6 and 22:47-48.

decisions.choice: the names set out in pairs, after "They were" (B) or "These were the twelve" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek list hangs on the first sentence. Balanced and Readable introduce it and group the names to make it easy to read.

decisions.choice: which means people who are sent out
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word, as the meaning decision does.

decisions.choice: the one who turned traitor (B); who later became a traitor (R)
decisions.reason: "Traitor" is the everyday word for one who betrays.

decisions.choice: Santiago for all three mentions of James, including Judas [hijo] de Santiago
decisions.reason: The term sheet's usual Spanish form for James. Using one form for every James keeps it plain that Judas's father bears the same name as the two apostles, which "Jacobo" in one place would hide; whether he is one of them is not said (meaning decision m5).

decisions.choice: el Zelote
decisions.reason: Luke uses the Greek word itself (meaning decision m4), so every level says "Zelote"; "cananista" in Matthew 10:4 renders the Aramaic form of the same name.

decisions.choice: Judas [fils] de Jacques (L); Jude, fils de Jacques (B, R); Judas Iscariot at every level
decisions.reason: The Greek gives both men the same name. Literal keeps it the same, so the reader sees it; Balanced and Readable follow the usual French custom of calling the first "Jude", which keeps him apart from Judas Iscariot.

decisions.choice: apôtres; douze in lowercase
decisions.reason: Here twelve is a number, not yet the title "les Douze" of the term sheet, so French writes it in lowercase, as Mark 3:14 does. Readable explains "apôtres" as the English Readable does (m1).

decisions.choice: mitume
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: "mtume" is one sent out with the authority of the one who sends him (meaning decision m1). Readable adds what the word means, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Mzelote
decisions.reason: Luke uses the Greek word itself (meaning decision m4), so every level says "Mzelote", the form Matthew's Readable uses; "Mkananayo" in Matthew 10:4 renders the Aramaic form of the same name.

decisions.choice: "sứ đồ" for apostles; "nghĩa là những người được sai đi" added at Readable
decisions.reason: "sứ đồ" is the Protestant word, used in Mark 6:30 and the letters; "tông đồ" is the Catholic one. Readable explains it, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "Xê-lốt" (L, B); "'người Nhiệt Thành'" (R)
decisions.reason: Luke's word is the Greek for "Zealot", where Mark 3:18 has the Aramaic form rendered "Ca-na-an". Literal and Balanced give the traditional transliteration; Readable says what the name means, as Mark's Readable does.

decisions.choice: "kẻ phản bội" (L, B); "đã phản bội" (R); "anh em" for Andrew's relation to Simon
decisions.reason: Luke's noun is "betrayer"; "kẻ phản bội" is the plain word for it. "anh em" leaves open whether Andrew was older or younger, as in Mark 1:16 and John 1:40.

decisions.choice: "열둘" (L), "열두 사람" (B, R); "사도" at every level, explained once (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the bare number, as "열둘" in Mark; Balanced and Readable say "열두 사람", since here they are picked out of the disciples, not yet named as a group. "사도" is the word of Mark 6:30 in Korean; Readable gives its meaning, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "열심당원" at every level; "야고보의 [아들] 유다" (L); "배반자" for prodotēs; Protestant name forms "바돌로매", "알패오", "가룟"
decisions.reason: Luke uses the Greek word for zealot, which Korean says with "열심당원" (Mark's Readable says it for "Cananaean"); the meaning decision gives both senses. The genitive "of James" is read as "son of" (meaning decision). "배반자" says what Luke's noun says.

source.text: Καὶ καταβὰς μετ’ αὐτῶν ἔστη ἐπὶ τόπου πεδινοῦ, καὶ ὄχλος πολὺς μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ, καὶ πλῆθος πολὺ τοῦ λαοῦ ἀπὸ πάσης τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ τῆς παραλίου Τύρου καὶ Σιδῶνος, οἳ ἦλθον ἀκοῦσαι αὐτοῦ καὶ ἰαθῆναι ἀπὸ τῶν νόσων αὐτῶν· καὶ οἱ ἐνοχλούμενοι ἀπὸ πνευμάτων ἀκαθάρτων ἐθεραπεύοντο·

records.literal_gloss: And having come down with them he stood on a place level, and a crowd large of disciples of him, and a multitude great of the people from all the Judea and Jerusalem and the coastal region of Tyre and Sidon, \v 18 who came to hear him and to be healed from the diseases of them; and those troubled by spirits unclean were being healed;

en.L: And coming down with them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stood on a level place, and [there was] a large crowd of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, and a great multitude of the people from all Judea and Jerusalem and the coast of Tyre and Sidon, \v 18 who came to hear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and to be healed of their diseases; and those troubled by unclean spirits were being healed.
en.B: Coming down the mountain with them, Jesus stood on a flat stretch of ground. A big crowd of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples had gathered there, along with a huge number of people who had come from every part of Judea, from Jerusalem, and from the seacoast near Tyre and Sidon. \v 18 They came to listen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and to be cured of their illnesses, and people tormented by unclean spirits were made well.
en.R: Jesus came down from the mountain with the apostles and stood on a flat place. A large group of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples was there. A great crowd of other people was there too. They came from all over Judea, from Jerusalem, and from the towns by the sea near Tyre and Sidon. \v 18 They came to listen to Jesus and to be healed of their sicknesses. Some had evil spirits that troubled them, and Jesus made them well.

es.L: Y bajando con ellos, se detuvo en un lugar llano, y [había] una gran multitud de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos y una gran muchedumbre del pueblo de toda Judea y Jerusalén y de la costa de Tiro y Sidón, \v 18 que vinieron a oírlo y a ser sanados de sus enfermedades; y los que eran atormentados por espíritus impuros eran sanados.
es.B: Jesús bajó del monte con ellos y se detuvo en un terreno llano. Allí se había reunido un gran grupo de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos, junto con una enorme cantidad de gente que había venido de todas partes de Judea, de Jerusalén y de la costa cercana a Tiro y Sidón. \v 18 Habían venido para escucharlo y para ser curados de sus enfermedades, y los que estaban atormentados por espíritus impuros quedaban sanos.
es.R: Jesús bajó del monte con los apóstoles y se detuvo en un lugar plano. Allí estaba un gran grupo de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos. También había mucha otra gente. Venían de toda Judea, de Jerusalén y de los pueblos junto al mar, cerca de Tiro y Sidón. \v 18 Vinieron a escuchar a Jesús y a ser sanados de sus enfermedades. Algunos tenían espíritus malignos que los atormentaban, y Jesús los sanaba.

fr.L: Et, étant descendu avec eux, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se tint en un lieu plat, et [il y avait] une grande foule de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples, et une grande multitude du peuple, de toute la Judée et de Jérusalem et du littoral de Tyr et de Sidon, \v 18 qui étaient venus pour {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}entendre et être guéris de leurs maladies ; et ceux qui étaient tourmentés par des esprits impurs étaient guéris.
fr.B: Jésus descendit de la montagne avec eux et s’arrêta sur un terrain plat. Une foule nombreuse de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples s’y trouvait, avec une très grande multitude de gens venus de toute la Judée, de Jérusalem et de la côte de Tyr et de Sidon. \v 18 Ils étaient venus pour {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}écouter et pour être guéris de leurs maladies, et ceux que tourmentaient des esprits impurs recouvraient la santé.
fr.R: Jésus est descendu de la montagne avec les apôtres et il s’est arrêté dans un endroit plat. Un grand groupe de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples était là. Une foule d’autres gens était là aussi. Ils venaient de toute la Judée, de Jérusalem, et des villes au bord de la mer, près de Tyr et de Sidon. \v 18 Ils étaient venus pour écouter Jésus et pour être guéris de leurs maladies. Certains avaient des esprits mauvais qui les tourmentaient, et Jésus les a guéris.

sw.L: Na akishuka pamoja nao, alisimama mahali tambarare, na [palikuwa na] umati mkubwa wa wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, na wingi mkubwa wa watu kutoka Uyahudi wote na Yerusalemu na pwani ya Tiro na Sidoni, \v 18 waliokuja kumsikiliza na kuponywa magonjwa yao; na wale waliosumbuliwa na pepo wachafu waliponywa.
sw.B: Yesu alishuka mlimani pamoja nao, akasimama mahali tambarare. Kundi kubwa la wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} lilikuwa limekusanyika pale, pamoja na umati mkubwa wa watu waliokuja kutoka kila sehemu ya Uyahudi, kutoka Yerusalemu, na kutoka pwani karibu na Tiro na Sidoni. \v 18 Walikuja kumsikiliza na kuponywa magonjwa yao, na wale walioteswa na pepo wachafu wakapona.
sw.R: Yesu alishuka kutoka mlimani pamoja na mitume, akasimama mahali tambarare. Kundi kubwa la wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} lilikuwa pale. Umati mkubwa wa watu wengine ulikuwa pale pia. Walitoka kila mahali katika Uyahudi, Yerusalemu, na miji ya pwani karibu na Tiro na Sidoni. \v 18 Walikuja kumsikiliza Yesu na kuponywa magonjwa yao. Baadhi yao walikuwa na pepo wabaya waliowasumbua, naye Yesu akawaponya.

vi.L: Và đi xuống với họ, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đứng trên một chỗ đất bằng, và [có] một đoàn đông các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và rất nhiều dân chúng từ khắp Giu-đê và Giê-ru-sa-lem và miền duyên hải Ty-rơ và Si-đôn, \v 18 là những người đã đến để nghe {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và để được chữa lành các bệnh tật của họ; và những người bị các linh ô uế quấy nhiễu cũng được chữa lành.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu cùng họ xuống núi và đứng trên một khoảng đất bằng. Ở đó có đông đảo các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, cùng rất nhiều người từ khắp miền Giu-đê, từ Giê-ru-sa-lem và từ miền ven biển Ty-rơ và Si-đôn. \v 18 Họ đến để nghe {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} giảng và để được chữa lành bệnh tật; những người bị linh ô uế hành hạ cũng được chữa lành.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu cùng các sứ đồ từ trên núi xuống và đứng ở một chỗ đất bằng. Có rất đông môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở đó. Cũng có rất nhiều người khác nữa. Họ đến từ khắp miền Giu-đê, từ thành Giê-ru-sa-lem, và từ các thành ven biển gần Ty-rơ và Si-đôn. \v 18 Họ đến để nghe Đức Giê-xu dạy và để được chữa lành bệnh. Có những người bị tà linh hành hạ, và Đức Giê-xu chữa lành cho họ.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 그들과 함께 내려오셔서 평평한 곳에 서셨다. 그리고 그분의 제자들의 큰 무리와, 온 유대와 예루살렘과 두로와 시돈의 해안 지방에서 온 백성의 큰 무리가 [있었다]. \v 18 그들은 그분의 말씀을 듣고 자기들의 병을 고침받으려고 온 사람들이었다. 그리고 더러운 영들에게 시달리는 사람들이 고침을 받고 있었다.
ko.B: 예수께서 그들과 함께 산에서 내려오셔서 평평한 곳에 서셨다. 그곳에는 예수의 제자들이 큰 무리를 이루고 있었고, 온 유대와 예루살렘과 두로와 시돈의 바닷가 지방에서 온 많은 백성도 있었다. \v 18 그들은 예수의 말씀을 듣고 병을 고침받으려고 왔다. 더러운 영들에게 시달리던 사람들도 나았다.
ko.R: 예수께서 사도들과 함께 산에서 내려오셔서 평평한 곳에 서셨다. 그곳에는 예수의 제자들이 많이 있었다. 다른 사람들도 아주 많이 와 있었다. 그들은 유대 온 지역과 예루살렘과 두로와 시돈 근처의 바닷가 마을들에서 왔다. \v 18 그들은 예수의 말씀을 듣고 병을 고침받으려고 왔다. 악한 영 때문에 괴로움을 당하던 사람들도 있었는데, 예수께서 그들을 고쳐 주셨다.

decisions.choice: a level place: a flat area, perhaps a plateau among the hills
alternatives: the plain at the foot of the mountain
decisions.reason: Jesus comes down from the mountain where he prayed (6:12) to a place level enough for a crowd. Matthew sets similar teaching on the mountain (Matthew 5:1); a level place on a hillside fits both.

decisions.choice: a large crowd ... and a great multitude: these have no verb of their own
decisions.reason: The sense is that they were there with him.

decisions.choice: Judea: probably the whole land of the Jews
alternatives: only the southern region around Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Luke sometimes uses Judea for the whole Jewish land (1:5; 4:44; 7:17).

decisions.choice: the coast of Tyre and Sidon: the Gentile port cities to the north
decisions.reason: Tyre and Sidon lay on the Phoenician coast, outside the Jewish land (compare 4:26). People came even from there.

decisions.choice: unclean spirits: demons
decisions.reason: Luke uses "unclean spirit" and "demon" for the same beings (4:33). They are named apart from the diseases.

decisions.choice: evil spirits
decisions.reason: "Unclean" here means opposed to God's holiness, not dirty. Readable says "evil".

decisions.choice: down the mountain (B); from the mountain (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where he came down from (6:12).

decisions.choice: Jesus made them well
decisions.reason: Readable names the healer; 6:19 makes clear that the power came from Jesus.

decisions.choice: espíritus impuros (L, B); espíritus malignos (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: demons (meaning decision m5). "Inmundo" is an older word many readers no longer use; Readable says "malignos", as the English Readable says "evil spirits".

decisions.choice: des esprits impurs (L, B); des esprits mauvais (R)
alternatives: des esprits impurs at every level
decisions.reason: "Un esprit impur" is the term sheet's form for Literal and Balanced; Readable follows the English "evil spirits", as in Mark, since "impur" here does not mean dirty (m5).

decisions.choice: pepo wachafu (L, B); pepo wabaya (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: these spirits are demons (meaning decision m5), and "pepo" says so plainly. Readable says "wabaya", as the English Readable says "evil spirits".

decisions.choice: "linh ô uế" (L, B); "tà linh" (R) for unclean spirits
decisions.reason: The settled terms for the Gospels, as in Mark 1:23 and Luke 4:36.

decisions.choice: "Giu-đê", "Ty-rơ", "Si-đôn"
decisions.reason: The Protestant forms, as in Mark 3:7-8.

decisions.choice: "더러운 영" (L, B); "악한 영" (R)
decisions.reason: The words settled for the unclean spirits in Mark and Luke 4 in Korean; Readable says "악한 영" (evil spirit), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "[있었다]" (L)
alternatives: leaving the crowds without a verb
decisions.reason: The two crowds have no verb of their own in the Greek (meaning decision); a Korean sentence cannot end without one, so Literal supplies it in brackets.

source.text: καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἐζήτουν ἅπτεσθαι αὐτοῦ, ὅτι δύναμις παρ’ αὐτοῦ ἐξήρχετο καὶ ἰᾶτο πάντας.

records.literal_gloss: And all the crowd were seeking to touch him, because power from him was going out and was healing all.

en.L: And all the crowd were seeking to touch {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, because power was going out from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and healing [them] all.
en.B: Everyone in the crowd kept trying to touch {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, since power flowed out from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and healed every one of them.
en.R: Everyone in the crowd tried to touch Jesus. Power was going out from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and it healed all of them.

es.L: Y toda la multitud procuraba tocarlo, porque un poder salía de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y sanaba a todos.
es.B: Toda la gente trataba de tocarlo, porque de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} salía poder y los sanaba a todos.
es.R: Toda la gente trataba de tocar a Jesús. De {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} salía poder, y ese poder los sanaba a todos.

fr.L: Et toute la foule cherchait à {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} toucher, parce qu’une puissance sortait de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et les guérissait tous.
fr.B: Tout le monde dans la foule essayait de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} toucher, car une puissance émanait de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et les guérissait tous, sans exception.
